run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR", "FATAL"] }` query and tell me how many hits come back. If that returns zero, find the right field for log severity and re-run the query.

report.summary: In index app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m the requested terms query on field `level` with values ERROR and FATAL returned 0 hits over the full authorized window (2026-10-24T18:10:57Z to 2026-11-23T18:10:57Z, @timestamp filter applied). The mapping of that index has no `level` field at all; its only properties are @timestamp (date), msg (text), severity_num (integer) and svc (keyword), so `level` does not exist as a field. The severity field is `severity_num`, and the severity label is also embedded in the `msg` text as a bracketed prefix. Re-running the same intent against the right field, terms: { severity_num: [5, 6] }, returned 8 hits; values 5 and 6 are shown by the documents to be the ERROR and FATAL severities (e.g. severity_num 5 with msg "[ERROR] DB timeout N", severity_num 6 with msg "[FATAL] Disk full N"). An independent check on the message text (query_string msg:ERROR OR msg:FATAL) also returned 8 hits. So: 0 hits for the requested `level` query, 8 hits for the correct severity field. Per-bucket distribution over the same window is severity_num 3 = 10, 4 = 5, 5 = 6, 6 = 2, for 23 documents total, all from svc order-276, with samples between 2026-11-23T18:06:01Z and 2026-11-23T18:09:10Z (that is the range the returned samples cover, not the whole window). This is a field-naming/schema observation only; whether these ERROR/FATAL lines indicate an incident was not investigated here.

claims.text: The requested query {"terms": {"level": ["ERROR", "FATAL"]}} against index app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m returned total 0 hits (relation eq) over the window 2026-10-24T18:10:57Z to 2026-11-23T18:10:57Z, with the @timestamp time filter applied and no shard failures.

The mapping of index app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m contains only @timestamp (date), msg (text), severity_num (integer) and svc (keyword); there is no `level` field in the mappings, which matches the 0-hit result of the requested query.

The severity field that exists and is populated is `severity_num`: a match_all query over the same window matched 23 documents with terms buckets severity_num 3 = 10 documents, 4 = 5, 5 = 6, 6 = 2 (sum_other_doc_count 0), and svc bucket order-276 = 23 documents.

Documents in app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m show severity_num 5 paired with messages prefixed "[ERROR]" (e.g. "[ERROR] DB timeout 1" at 2026-11-23T18:06:01Z) and severity_num 6 paired with "[FATAL]" (e.g. "[FATAL] Disk full 1" at 2026-11-23T18:07:01Z); severity_num 4 carries "[WARN] Slow query" and 3 carries "[INFO] Order placed". All 23 returned documents are svc order-276, spanning 2026-11-23T18:06:01Z to 2026-11-23T18:09:10Z.

Re-running the same intent on the correct field, terms: { severity_num: [5, 6] }, returned 8 hits over the same window, of which 6 are severity_num 5 (ERROR) and 2 are severity_num 6 (FATAL) according to the bucket counts.
An independent check on the message text, query_string "msg:ERROR OR msg:FATAL", also returned 8 hits over the same window, corroborating that 8 ERROR/FATAL records exist in this index in the window.

Index app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m exists, is green/open, and reports docs.count 23 with store.size 6.8kb as of the query time; this count is the index state at query time, not a count inside the incident window.

The 8 ERROR/FATAL records visible in this index (6 "[ERROR] DB timeout", 2 "[FATAL] Disk full", svc order-276, samples 2026-11-23T18:06-18:09Z) may indicate a genuine dependency or disk problem for order-276, but no service-level error rate, trace error spans or Kubernetes pod state was examined here, so impact and cause remain unverified.

Query log severity in this index on severity_num using numeric values (3=INFO, 4=WARN, 5=ERROR, 6=FATAL, as observed in the mapped documents) rather than on a `level` field, or use a query_string on the msg text where the bracketed severity prefix is written; if a `level`-named field is required, the index would need a mapping/ingest change, which was not authorised here.

gaps: The 0-hit result for field `level` shows only that this query matched nothing; the reason is supported separately by the index mapping, which has no `level` property. Whether the 8 ERROR/FATAL lines correspond to an actual incident, and their downstream or customer impact, was not investigated: no Prometheus error-rate/latency series, Jaeger error spans or Kubernetes pod/workload state for order-276 was queried in this run.

The 23 documents (and the 8 ERROR/FATAL ones) are all timestamped 2026-11-23T18:06:01Z-18:09:10Z in the returned sample; earlier behaviour inside the 30-day authorized window was not sampled, so no trend or onset time can be stated.
